newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BRL warns of sales/volume pressures.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BRL warns of sales/volume pressures.

text.p: Premium winemaker BRL Hardy Ltd said on Thursday that it expected industry sales to increase in the short term but warned of price and volume pressures over the medium term.

"BRL Hardy is well positioned to meet such competition and to take advantage of opportunities which may arise both in Australia and overseas," the company said in a statement accompanying its 1995/96 profit result. Net profit in the year to June 30 jumped by 51.8 percent to A$10.64 million.
It unsuccessfully bid earlier this year for fellow winemaker Rothbury, now owned by Foster's Brewing Group Ltd.
The company said it was disappointed it did not acquire Rothbury but made a A$2 million net profit on the sale of Rothbury shares to Foster's unit Mildara.
"The company is considering a number of other opportunities which are compatible with our strategies and consistent with continuing growth both in Australia and overseas," it said.

BRL Hardy said while the wine industry should increase domestic and international sales in the short term, the company was alert to the "potential risks of grape surpluses (especially white varieties) over the next two years as new vineyards come into bearing".
"Export sales may take some time to absorb the surplus and it is possible that significant price competition may result in the domestic market," BRL Hardy said.
"Offsetting this is an expected reduction in grape prices from 1997 which should assist in reducing costs of production."
